newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai baht firms, interbank drops late.
newsitem.headline: Thai baht firms, interbank drops late.

text.p: The Thai baht firmed late on Wednesday amid dollar profit-taking as the greenback dipped against majors in overseas markets, trade sources said.
The news of Moody's downgrade of Thailand's foreign currency long-term debt rating had a very brief and limited impact on the currency as the news had long been discounted by the market, they said.
The baht edged up to 26.080/100 (bid/offer) to the dollar in the late trade from 26.106/109 early.

"Market players sold the dollar for the baht when it started to decline because of a comment by a senior Japanese official. But I think the overall trend of the dollar is still bullish," said a dealer from a US bank here.
The dollar/baht traded in a narrow high-low range of 26.117 and 26.007.
The overnight interbank rate also dropped further to 8.50-9.00 percent from 9.00-9.50 percent this morning as more baht entered the system through dollar/baht swap deals.
"Lots of people borrowed through the the swap market as the premium was quite attractive," said a local bank dealer.

"More money will enter the market soon from the dollar selling in the spot market and the (interbank) rate is likely to be low until people start withdrawing money for the New Year holiday," he added.
The one-month dollar baht swap premium fell to 6.00/7.00 satang late Wednesday from 6.55/7.55 early.
